# MechanicDB — Automotive OBD-II Diagnostic & Repair Database

> A structured dataset mapping 15,886 verified OBD-II Diagnostic Trouble Codes (9,249 SAE-standard + 6,637 manufacturer-specific across 32 makes) to 56,561 ranked repair procedures with DIY difficulty ratings, aftermarket parts-cost ranges (USD), labor-hour estimates, step-by-step instructions, and 75,055 replacement-parts mappings, organized into 647 hand-authored fault families.

## What it is
- One row per trouble code (SAE rows unique by `dtc_code`; OEM rows unique by `(oem_make, dtc_code)`), joined to authored procedures and parts. The supported legacy field `probability_rank` gives procedure consideration order within a code (`1` = first), conditional on prerequisites and findings; it is not measured cause likelihood, repair success, severity, urgency or minimum cost. Machine-readable context: https://mechanicdb.dataengineered.io/ordering_metadata.json
- Every fix carries `difficulty_level` (Easy DIY / Moderate DIY / Professional Required), `est_parts_cost_min/max_usd`, `est_labor_hours`, and ` • `-separated step-by-step instructions.
- Code definitions originate in SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 (MIT-licensed upstream compilation, attribution preserved); repair content is original editorial material from a deterministic, test-gated build pipeline. Costs are editorial estimates, not quotes.
- Formats: pipe-delimited UTF-8-BOM CSV, Snappy Parquet (92.0% smaller), SQLite (full dataset).

## Key pages
- [Landing & pricing](https://mechanicdb.dataengineered.io/): what's inside, schema, interactive DTC decoder, and how to buy.
- [Free sample on GitHub](https://github.com/MechanicDB/MechanicDB-public): 90 codes (75 SAE + 15 OEM) in the identical schema, ODbL v1.0.
- [Free sample on Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dataengineered/mechanicdb-automotive-obd2-repair-database): same sample with metadata.
- [J1939 fault code database](https://mechanicdb.dataengineered.io/j1939-fault-code-database): the Heavy Duty tier — 4,212 SAE J1939 SPN/FMI fault pairs from 16 published OEM documents across 10 manufacturers, coverage by OEM and system, the 32-entry J1939 FMI reference, sample rows; one page per OEM under https://mechanicdb.dataengineered.io/j1939/ (e.g. /j1939/eaton, /j1939/wabco, /j1939/john-deere).
- [Fault code statistics](https://mechanicdb.dataengineered.io/stats/): codes by vehicle system and make, code strings shared across makes, fault families, DIY difficulty of the ranked fixes, parts-cost and labor-hour estimates, most-mapped parts, computed from the full catalogue (catalogue statistics, not road incidence); CC BY 4.0, with [data.json](https://mechanicdb.dataengineered.io/stats/data.json) and embeddable SVG charts.

## Pricing & licensing
- Free sample: 90 codes, ODbL v1.0.
- Standard: $49 one-time — 9,249 SAE codes, 32,767 fixes, 44,588 parts, CSV + Parquet + SQLite, commercial license, instant download.
- OEM Complete: $149 one-time — full merged dataset (15,886 codes incl. 32 makes' OEM codes), commercial license, instant download.
- Fault & Recall bundle: $179 one-time (vs $198 separately) — OEM Complete + RecallDB Vehicle (NHTSA vehicle & equipment recalls, CSV + Parquet + SQLite) + a bundle-only bulletin index (NHTSA service bulletins that cite each trouble code, with their vehicles), instant downloads after one checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/3cI3cw1cQevsazVaaA3840h
- Heavy Duty (J1939): $149 one-time, standalone — SAE J1939 SPN+FMI fault pairs from published OEM fault tables (Eaton, WABCO, Bendix, John Deere, Navistar, Cummins, Caterpillar, PSI, Perkins, Yanmar) with ranked fixes and part mappings, CSV + Parquet + SQLite, commercial license, instant download: https://buy.stripe.com/6oUeVef3G2MK5fB3Mc3840j — 100-fault free sample in `samples/heavyduty/`, ODbL v1.0, schema in DATA_DICTIONARY.md section 6.
- Commercial license: https://mechanicdb.dataengineered.io/license — Standard, OEM Complete and Heavy Duty share the same terms (grant, restrictions, warranty, termination); each tier's copy names its own product, use cases and data sources.
- Contact: mechanicdb@dataengineered.io
- Not a substitute for SAE J2012 or its Digital Annex (J2012DA): those are licensed per seat and are never redistributed here. MechanicDB reproduces no SAE document text, carries no Failure Type Bytes, and is not a citable normative reference — it is a factual code-to-meaning and code-to-repair compilation. For the standard itself, use the SAE store, Techstreet, the ANSI Webstore, Accuris, a university engineering library's SAE Digital Library subscription, or the harmonized ISO 15031-6 from a national standards body.
- Repair steps are educational reference material, not professional repair advice; high-voltage and SRS/airbag work requires qualified technicians.

- Stable identity contract (prepared cutover): IDENTITY.md; qualified domain/entity references, filtered sample companions, immutable release IDs and ambiguity-safe legacy migration.
